# SK9003 — A style option was set in `skala.jsonc`

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A property somewhere in `skala.jsonc` resolves to an option in the registry. Style is configured in `.editorconfig` and nowhere else (ADR-001), so the property was ignored, and `skala config check` fails on it without `--strict`. Move the line into `.editorconfig` as `key = value`; the detail names the canonical key and its tier.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tool |
| Default severity | error |
| Scope | Compilation |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.1 |

## Why

One style language, because two is how the IDE and the gate come to disagree: a value in `skala.jsonc` is invisible to Rider, so the code would format one way under the IDE and another under Skala. Aliases resolve too — `max_line_length` in `skala.jsonc` fires as readily as `skala_max_line_length` — and the detail gives the spelling to use in `.editorconfig`.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
{ "skala_max_line_length": 120 }
```

Write:

```csharp
[*.cs]
skala_max_line_length = 120
```

## When it does not fire

The walk over the document is recursive and unscoped, so a registry key nested under `gates`, `canonical` or inside an array is reported as well. A `skala.jsonc` that does not parse reports `SK9007` instead and nothing here. The diagnostic carries the file and no line, because the JSON reader does not keep one.
